title: When the Oath Turns
premise: Coral Dunmore has spent her life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow, stealing memories from travelers to sell to the memory-brokers who keep the settlement fed. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands and whispers that she is the thirteenth keeper, Coral discovers the map leads beyond the valley's edge — to the Oathstone, an artifact whose theft centuries ago broke a truce between humankind and the fae courts. Hunted by both a royal inquisitor and a fae lord who each want her secret, Coral must decide whether restoring the stone will end the coming war or hand one side absolute power. In the end she shatters the Oathstone rather than return it, freeing magic back into the world at large and choosing exile over belonging — but carrying, for the first time, memories that are truly her own.
about_author: Emrys Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forgotten folk ballads before turning to fiction. They write about outsiders, oaths, and the small betrayals that hold communities together.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV Coral. On market day, Coral lifts a soldier's memory of his daughter's funeral and sells it to broker Maghda, feeling nothing but the familiar hollowness after. The chapter establishes the Hollow's economy of stolen pasts and Coral's rule: never keep what you take. Emotional beat: numb competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A wounded man collapses at the valley ford, clutching a leather map case; his blood smells faintly of iron and lilac, wrong for the Hollow. He presses the case into Coral's hands and dies saying 'thirteenth.' Emotional beat: dread — the first crack in her sealed-off life.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The map refuses to burn or tear, and ink crawls across it when no one watches. Maghda offers a fortune for it; Coral lies for the first time in her career. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, terrifying taste of possessing something instead of passing it on.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Wren Vael, royal inquisitor, arrives under a flag of courtesy, asking gentle questions about a missing courier. His politeness is worse than threats; he already knows someone in the Hollow helped. Coral watches him work and understands he will not leave empty-handed. Emotional beat: cold fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: POV Coral. An old hedge-witch reads the map's marginalia: the courier was the twelfth keeper, killed by something that hunts keepers, and the moon completes its thirteenth turn in one season. Coral realizes the valley's magic-dead soil isn't protection — it's a cage built around people like her. Emotional beat: grief for a childhood built on a lie.

chapters.title: Leaving Is a Kind of Dying
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral slips out at dawn through the scree pass, looking back once at the only home she's known. Beyond the boundary line, the air hums, colors deepen, and a stray thought of hers flickers visible as light. Emotional beat: vertigo and wonder tangled together.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The map pulls her along roads that shift behind her; she survives an ambush by bandits using a stolen memory of swordplay, and hates how easily violence fits. She meets Tam, a runaway tinker's boy tailing her for the story. Emotional beat: reluctant companionship against instinct.

chapters.title: Lord of the Lilac Court
chapters.summary: POV Coral (with interlude from the fae lord Ashvael). Ashvael intercepts her, courteous and terrifying, offering safe passage in exchange for the map. He reveals the fae did not steal the Oathstone — they were robbed of it — but his court's justice means a human debt paid in human years. Emotional beat: seduction of an easy bargain.

chapters.title: Bargains and Small Mercies
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral refuses Ashvael and flees with Tam through the Weeping Woods, where trees show strangers their worst memories. Tam sees hers — the memory she stole from herself long ago — and doesn't flinch. Emotional beat: shame met with unexpected grace.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Keeper's Grave
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Following the map backward, they find the courier's shallow grave and his journal: he wasn't delivering the map, he was running from the inquisition, which wants the Oathstone reforged under crown control. Coral understands Wren Vael's hunt is sanctioned. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: City of Scales
chapters.summary: POV Coral. In the free city of Verrin, where anything can be bought, Coral seeks a scholar of oaths and finds corruption instead — the brokers' guild here is a sisterhood to Maghda's, and her face is already on a bounty sheet. Tam covers her escape and is taken. Emotional beat: guilt; the cost of being followed.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs Off the Books
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Imprisoned by guild enforcers, Tam bargains with a disgraced guild clerk, trading testimony for Coral's whereabouts staying quiet. He learns the clerk keeps a ledger of every oath broken by the powerful — a private court of paper. Emotional beat: discovering that justice outside the law is built by ordinary stubborn people.

chapters.title: The Hunt on the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Wren Vael corners Coral on the salt flats; their duel is fought half with blades, half with truths, as he argues order requires the stone and she argues order built on theft is just theft with banners. She escapes wounded, having seen genuine conviction in him. Emotional beat: doubt — the enemy is not a monster.

chapters.title: Ashvael's Patience Ends
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Ashvael saves her from Vael's soldiers, then names his price: the map now, or he takes her memories one by one until nothing of Coral remains. She gives him a decoy memory woven from stolen fragments, buying days and self-loathing. Emotional beat: becoming the thing she despises to survive.

chapters.title: Rescue Written in a Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Tam and Coral. The clerk's network springs Tam free and smuggles both of them toward the Oathstone's resting place beneath the ruined Abbey of First Light. Coral begins returning stolen memories to strangers along the road, lighter with each release. Emotional beat: restitution as healing.

chapters.title: The Abbey of First Light
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Beneath the abbey, the Oathstone waits in a chamber where every broken vow ever sworn echoes audibly. Coral touches it and receives the full memory of the original theft: humans stole the stone first, out of desperation during a famine. Emotional beat: the collapse of every simple story she's been told.

chapters.title: Three Banners at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Vael's crown troops, Ashvael's fae host, and the guild's hired swords converge on the abbey as the thirteenth moon rises. Each faction offers Coral legitimacy, safety, vengeance — everything except the choice itself. Emotional beat: claustrophobic pressure before the break.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: POV Coral. At moonrise, with all three factions breaching the crypt, Coral must place the stone in one claimant's hands. Instead she drives her thief's pick into its heart, shattering it, releasing magic into every living thing equally. The shockwave unmakes the crypt; Tam drags her out. Emotional beat: terrible liberation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Broken Oath
chapters.summary: POV multiple brief vignettes. Magic spreads unpredictably: crops quicken, some sicken, the powerless find power, the powerful find limits. Vael kneels in the ruins, his certainty broken; Ashvael laughs for the first time in a century. Emotional beat: awe and disorientation at a world remade.

chapters.title: Judgment Without a Throne
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Captured by the surviving factions, Coral faces a makeshift tribunal — Vael arguing law, Ashvael arguing debt, the clerk reading her acts aloud from the ledger. Tam testifies. The verdict: exile, not execution, because the ledger shows more mercy than crime. Emotional beat: justice rendered by people, not crowns.

chapters.title: Memories of My Own
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Before leaving, Coral returns the last stolen memory she carried — the one she took from herself as a child — and finally knows why she could never leave the Hollow: she had sworn an oath there at seven years old, and oaths bound even where magic didn't. Now unbound, she grieves and heals. Emotional beat: bittersweet wholeness.

chapters.title: Where the Map Ends
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral and Tam walk out beyond the last marked border, the blank map now slowly filling with new ink under her fingers — roads no one has named. She carries no stolen memories, no master, no oath, only the secret of what she chose and the company she kept. Emotional beat: open-horizon hope earned through loss.
